packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-13 - unverified blind image reading

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or earlier reading of these leaves. My standing context mentions that a Fragmentarium/Stams project exists, but gives no reading or identification for this item. I opened only PROMPT.md and the image files (I also listed the packet directory, which shows packet.json; I did not open it). I did not search, consult editions, or identify the work. Saints' names below are transcribed because they are written on the leaves, not inferred.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Overviews: image-001 (two faces: left leaf pencilled "Stams, STA, Frg. 107-2r", right leaf "107-1r") and image-008 (left "107-2v", right "107-1v"). Two small separate leaves, each about 9.5 x 13 cm on the scale, upright orientation, one column of about 25-29 lines.
- Tiles: 002 = 2r upper left; 003 = 2r upper right + left edge of 1r; 004 = 1r upper; 005 = 2r lower left; 006 = 2r lower right + 1r lower left edge; 007 = 1r lower; 009 = 2v upper left; 010 = 2v upper right + 1v upper left; 011 = 1v upper right; 012 = 2v lower left; 013 = 2v lower right + 1v lower left; 014 = 1v lower right. The tiles overlap; lines repeated across tiles are counted once below.
- Black ink text with red rubrics and red cue letters, red and blue (often faded) two-line initials; on 2v many lines are underlined/ruled in red. Text and rubrics alternate: rubrics such as "Ad v(esperas)", "sup(er) ps(almos)", "An(tiphona)", "R(esponsoriu)m" (written R with superscript m), "V(ersus)" (crossed V), "ps", "Oratio", "Cap(itulum)", "ymnus", "Ad Mat(utinum) Invit(atorium)", "In p(ri)mo / 2o / 3o noct(urno)", "Ad laudes", "Sup(er) Mag(nifica)t", "In s(ecun)dis v(esperis)". Tentative interpretation: liturgical office (antiphons, responsories, versicles, collect) for a saint's feast; the rubric heading on 2r names the occasion. No running titles, no glosses. Offset/ghost text from another page is visible in the lower margins of 2r and the top of 1r (not part of these pages). Pinholes and edge losses at top left of 2r and right edge of 1r; a hole on the left edge of 1v at about lines 24-27.
- A loose large red letter (a "B"/"R"-like form) sits in the lower margin of 1v below the text (image-014); it may be a partly erased or unrelated initial.

Conventions: (..) expansion; "?" after an uncertain reading; [illegible]; [red ..] / [blue ..] for coloured letters. Line numbers count text lines from the top of the named tile (the heading counts as line 1). Columns: single column throughout.
